digest.headline: Les benchmarks d'agents LLM et l'optimisation des architectures dominent la recherche en IA, avec des avancées majeures en évaluation processuelle et en efficacité computationnelle
digest.overview: La veille du 19 octobre 2026 met en lumière des travaux centrés sur l'amélioration des capacités des agents LLM dans des environnements dynamiques, ainsi que des optimisations architecturales réduisant drastiquement les coûts tout en préservant les performances. Les approches processuelles et l'interprétabilité des mécanismes internes gagnent en importance face aux limites des évaluations basées sur les résultats finaux.

highlights.title: Évaluation processuelle des agents LLM en marchés évolutifs
highlights.text: LiveMACEBench introduit un benchmark évaluant les agents LLM dans des marchés financiers réels, en analysant leurs processus internes (outils, mémoire, collaboration) plutôt que les résultats bruts. Cette approche révèle un écart significatif entre capacités mécanistiques et performances réalisées, offrant des diagnostics précis via l'analyse des traces d'exécution. Elle répond à un besoin croissant d'évaluer la robustesse des agents dans des environnements dynamiques et non stationnaires.

highlights.title: Optimisation radicale des embeddings et architectures en boucle
highlights.text: Deux travaux marquants réduisent les coûts computationnels : (1) Un tableau d'embeddings gelé de 16 Mo permet de compresser des modèles comme Gemma 3 270M à 46 Mo sans perte de performance, accélérant l'inférence CPU. (2) LEV et l'étude sur les modèles en boucle (Huginn) améliorent la précision avec une profondeur dynamique, économisant jusqu'à 24% de calcul. Ces méthodes ciblent des gains d'efficacité critiques pour le déploiement à grande échelle.

highlights.title: Amélioration de la robustesse et de la récupération des agents
highlights.text: BELIEFWEAVER combine mise à jour de croyances relationnelles et modèles du monde implicites pour les agents long-horizon, améliorant les scores de 5,1 à 9,8 points tout en réduisant les coûts d'inférence de 54,8%. Parallèlement, FC-SWE et Dream2Discern intègrent les retours d'échecs et génèrent des exemples difficiles pour renforcer la résilience des systèmes multi-agents. Ces travaux adressent des défis clés en fiabilité et généralisation.

highlights.title: Interprétabilité et supervision des mécanismes internes
highlights.text: Belief-Trajectory Energy (BTE) et Lexical Reference Frames offrent des outils pour analyser les révisions prédictives couche par couche et interpréter les états cachés des LLM. OPMD étend la distillation en supervisant les mécanismes intermédiaires, surpassant les méthodes existantes. Ces avancées répondent à un besoin croissant de transparence et de contrôle des processus décisionnels des modèles.

highlights.title: Benchmarks spécialisés pour agents mobiles et multimodaux
highlights.text: OpenMobile-2 propose un environnement simulé avec 110+ apps et 12K trajectoires pour évaluer les agents mobiles, tandis que SABER teste la robustesse des modèles vision-langage en compositionnalité. Ces benchmarks révèlent des limites persistantes en généralisation et en conservation des liens attribut-objet, guidant les efforts futurs en supervision multimodale et en interaction avec des environnements complexes.

digest.trend: La recherche en IA se recentre sur l'optimisation des architectures et des processus internes, avec une emphase croissante sur l'évaluation processuelle, l'interprétabilité et la robustesse des agents dans des environnements dynamiques. Les gains d'efficacité computationnelle et les benchmarks spécialisés deviennent des leviers clés pour dépasser les limites des approches basées sur les résultats finaux.

items.title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets
items.summary: Evaluating agents by outcomes alone can obscure the capabilities that produce them. This problem is especially pronounced in evolving environments, where outcomes reflect a closed-loop interaction between agent behavior and changing external conditions. We introduce LiveMACEBench, a process-aware benchmark that uses live financial markets as a naturally evolving testbed for persistent LLM agents. Five frontier LLMs operate along continuous trajectories under matched Tool Use, Persistent Memory, Rule Following, and Multi-Agent Collaboration configurations. We evaluate them through both realized outcomes and mechanism-specific diagnostics derived from complete decision traces. Across 30 days of live evaluation, we find a pronounced outcome-capability gap: realized returns often diverge from capability-specific measurements, and similar outcomes can arise from markedly different patterns of mechanism use. Trace-level diagnostics further expose distinct bottlenecks across capabilities, demonstrating that mechanism access, effective mechanism use, and downstream performance are not interchangeable measures of agent capability. LiveMACEBench makes this distinction measurable, turning live markets from a performance leaderboard into a diagnostic environment for agent capability
items.tldr: LiveMACEBench évalue les agents LLM dans des marchés financiers réels avec un focus sur les processus internes (outils, mémoire, règles, collaboration) plutôt que sur les résultats bruts. Met en évidence un écart entre capacités mécanistiques et performances réalisées, avec des diagnostics au niveau des traces.

deep_analysis.probleme: L'évaluation des agents basés sur les LLMs se limite souvent à des résultats finaux (outcomes), ce qui masque les capacités réelles sous-jacentes, surtout dans des environnements dynamiques comme les marchés financiers. Cette approche ne permet pas de distinguer si un bon ou mauvais résultat provient de l'efficacité de l'agent ou de conditions externes changeantes, ni d'identifier les mécanismes spécifiques responsables des performances.
deep_analysis.methode: LiveMACEBench propose un benchmark *process-aware* utilisant les marchés financiers en temps réel comme environnement évolutif pour évaluer des agents LLMs persistants. Cinq modèles de pointe (frontier LLMs) sont testés sur des trajectoires continues avec des configurations contrôlées pour quatre capacités : *Tool Use* (utilisation d'outils), *Persistent Memory* (mémoire persistante), *Rule Following* (respect des règles) et *Multi-Agent Collaboration* (collaboration multi-agents). L'évaluation combine des métriques de résultats (ex. rendements financiers) et des diagnostics spécifiques aux mécanismes, extraits de traces complètes des décisions. Les agents opèrent pendant 30 jours en conditions réelles, avec une analyse fine des interactions entre comportements et évolutions du marché.
deep_analysis.resultats: Les résultats révèlent un *outcome-capability gap* marqué : les rendements réalisés divergent souvent des mesures de capacités spécifiques, et des performances similaires peuvent émerger de schémas d'utilisation des mécanismes radicalement différents. Les diagnostics au niveau des traces montrent des goulots d'étranglement distincts selon les capacités, confirmant que l'accès à un mécanisme, son utilisation efficace et la performance finale ne sont pas des indicateurs interchangeables. Par exemple, un agent peut bien suivre des règles mais échouer à exploiter des outils, ou inversement.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les modèles LLMs testés ni les détails techniques des configurations (ex. architecture des outils, implémentation de la mémoire persistante). L'évaluation sur 30 jours, bien que longue pour un benchmark, reste limitée pour généraliser les conclusions à d'autres environnements dynamiques. Enfin, l'absence de comparaison avec des méthodes d'évaluation traditionnelles (ex. benchmarks statiques) rend difficile l'appréciation de l'apport réel de LiveMACEBench.
deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante d'évaluation *process-aware* des agents LLMs, mais son applicabilité au-delà des marchés financiers et sa robustesse méthodologique restent à valider par des études complémentaires.

items.title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
items.summary: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed. We ask what that table actually buys. We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it. The learned table buys 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, but on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA the frozen-table model is better or tied; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table. With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory. The frozen table wins by 1.7 to 2.3 nats on rare words, accepts 10,000 new words after training with a 3% cost where the learned table collapses by 43%, and all of it is released with the weights, the data and every evaluation answer.
items.tldr: Remplacement de la table d'embeddings par un tableau gelé de 16 Mo (512-bit codes) dans des petits modèles (Gemma 3 270M, BitNet b1.58), réduisant la taille du modèle à 46 Mo tout en maintenant les performances (voire amélioration sur certains benchmarks) et en accélérant l'inférence (615-740 tok/s sur CPU).

deep_analysis.probleme: Les modèles de langage de petite taille souffrent d'une inefficacité majeure : leur table d'embeddings (vocabulaire) représente une part disproportionnée des paramètres totaux (ex. 63% pour Gemma 3 270M). Cette table, souvent laissée en 16 bits même après quantification, alourdit inutilement la taille du modèle et limite les gains en performance et en efficacité computationnelle, notamment pour des applications embarquées ou sur CPU.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs proposent de remplacer la table d'embeddings apprise par une table *gelée* de 16 Mo, sans paramètres entraînables. Cette table est générée une fois pour toutes à partir d'un embedding pré-entraîné, via une projection en composantes principales (PCA) suivie d'une binarisation des signes (512 bits par token). Le modèle (de type Gemma) est ensuite entraîné *from scratch* avec cette table fixe, en comparant les performances avec et sans elle. Une variante utilise un corps ternaire (BitNet b1.58) pour réduire davantage la taille et accélérer l'inférence. La méthode permet aussi d'ajouter dynamiquement de nouveaux mots post-entraînement avec un coût minimal.
deep_analysis.resultats: La table apprise n'apporte qu'un gain marginal de 0,20 nats en perte de validation pour 2,6 fois plus de paramètres entraînables. Sur les benchmarks (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA), le modèle avec table gelée performe aussi bien, voire mieux, que la version standard, sauf sur ARC-Easy. Avec BitNet, le modèle complet pèse 46 Mo, génère 615 à 740 tokens/seconde sur CPU (5-6x plus rapide qu'un modèle float quantifié en 8 bits), et utilise 7 fois moins de mémoire. La table gelée améliore aussi la robustesse aux mots rares (+1,7 à 2,3 nats) et permet d'ajouter 10 000 mots post-entraînement avec une dégradation de seulement 3% (contre 43% pour la table apprise).
deep_analysis.limites: L'étude se limite à un modèle de taille modeste (270M paramètres) et un corpus d'entraînement restreint (2,05 milliards de tokens), ce qui peut biaiser les résultats pour des modèles plus grands ou des tâches spécialisées. La binarisation des embeddings pourrait aussi introduire des artefacts pour des tokens sémantiquement proches mais binaires éloignés. Enfin, la généralisation à d'autres architectures (ex. transformers avec attention différente) n'est pas évaluée.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette approche mérite une attention particulière pour les applications où l'efficacité mémoire et la vitesse d'inférence sont critiques, mais son impact sur des modèles plus grands ou des tâches complexes reste à démontrer.

items.title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Long-horizon agents often struggle to recover from failures whose causes lie several steps earlier, beyond what local reflection or backtracking can resolve. We introduce BELIEFWEAVER, a framework that combines persistent evidence across attempts with prospective reasoning over repair directions. It maintains a relational belief state over frontiers, attempts, observations, and checkpoints. Execution evidence updates related frontier priorities across attempts and rollback, while diagnostic evidence gates execution. An implicit world model (IWM) evaluates repair hypotheses, predicts progress, and identifies relations among frontiers to guide exploration. We further distill these recurring IWM reasoning components into a 9B student through supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation (OPD). Across three terminal-based benchmarks, BELIEFWEAVER improves aggregate final score by 5.1 percentage points over native Terminus-2 continuation, with positive trends in exploration efficiency. The distilled 9B student improves final score by 9.8 percentage points over the reported native baseline while reducing estimated teacher API cost by 54.8% relative to the matched teacher. These results show that persistent evidence and prospective reasoning can improve recovery in long-horizon agent tasks while substantially reducing reliance on teacher-model inference.
items.tldr: Présentation de BELIEFWEAVER, un framework pour agents long-horizon combinant mise à jour de croyances relationnelles et modèle du monde implicite (IWM), avec distillation supervisée et OPD. Améliore les scores de 5,1 à 9,8 points selon les benchmarks, tout en réduisant les coûts d'inférence de 54,8%.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les agents à horizon long rencontrent des difficultés majeures pour se remettre d'échecs dont les causes remontent à plusieurs étapes antérieures, au-delà de ce que peuvent corriger des mécanismes locaux de réflexion ou de retour en arrière. Ces échecs persistants limitent leur capacité à accomplir des tâches complexes nécessitant une planification étendue et une adaptation dynamique aux imprévus.
deep_analysis.methode: BELIEFWEAVER est un cadre qui combine la persistance des preuves collectées lors des tentatives précédentes avec un raisonnement prospectif pour orienter les réparations. Il maintient un état de croyance relationnel structuré autour de frontières (frontiers), tentatives, observations et points de contrôle. Les preuves d'exécution mettent à jour les priorités des frontières entre les tentatives et les retours en arrière, tandis que les preuves diagnostiques filtrent l'exécution. Un modèle de monde implicite (IWM) évalue les hypothèses de réparation, prédit les progrès et identifie les relations entre les frontières pour guider l'exploration. Enfin, les composants récurrents du raisonnement de l'IWM sont distillés dans un modèle étudiant de 9 milliards de paramètres via un fine-tuning supervisé et une distillation en ligne (OPD).
deep_analysis.resultats: Sur trois benchmarks basés sur des terminaux, BELIEFWEAVER améliore le score final agrégé de 5,1 points de pourcentage par rapport à la continuation native de Terminus-2. Le modèle étudiant distillé de 9B améliore ce score de 9,8 points de pourcentage par rapport à la baseline native rapportée, tout en réduisant les coûts estimés d'inférence du modèle enseignant de 54,8 % par rapport à l'enseignant apparié. Ces résultats indiquent une amélioration de l'efficacité d'exploration et une réduction significative de la dépendance aux modèles enseignants coûteux.
deep_analysis.limites: Le document ne détaille pas explicitement les limites du cadre, mais on peut supposer que la généralisation à des environnements très dynamiques ou non structurés reste un défi. De plus, la dépendance à un modèle de monde implicite pourrait introduire des biais ou des erreurs de prédiction difficiles à diagnostiquer. Enfin, l'efficacité de la distillation pourrait varier selon la complexité des tâches et la qualité des données d'entraînement.
deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante combinant persistance des preuves et raisonnement prospectif, offrant des gains tangibles en performance et en efficacité pour les agents à horizon long.

items.title: OPMD: On-Policy Mechanism Distillation Beyond Output Supervision
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves language-model by supervising a student on prefixes sampled from its own policy, but its supervision remains confined to the output space. Consequently, OPD transfers what a teacher predicts without supervising the intermediate computation that produces those predictions. Simply distilling intermediate representations like representation matching is insufficient since teacher and student representations may differ geometrically, and even well-aligned hidden states need not be usable by the student's subsequent computation. We introduce On-Policy Mechanism Distillation (OPMD), which transfers teacher-derived intermediate computation while explicitly accounting for its compatibility with the student. OPMD first constructs a student-compatible teacher that transforms teacher representations into intermediate states usable by the student's downstream computation, then it internalizes these states from on-policy trajectories. OPMD achieves the highest average accuracy among the evaluated distillation baselines in all three teacher--student settings, and generalizes to multi-teacher distillation and cross-family supervised fine-tuning. Further analyses show that mechanism supervision yields more effective reasoning and meaningfully alters the student's intermediate computation and solution strategies, supporting that it transfers information beyond output supervision alone. Together, these results establish mechanism-level supervision as an effective way to move on-policy distillation beyond output supervision, enabling students to learn inner mechanisms they can use and internalize.
items.tldr: OPMD étend l'on-policy distillation (OPD) en supervisant non seulement les sorties mais aussi les mécanismes intermédiaires compatibles avec l'étudiant. Surpasse les baselines existantes en distillation, y compris multi-enseignants et cross-family SFT, avec des gains significatifs en précision.

deep_analysis.probleme: La distillation de modèles (OPD) améliore les performances d'un modèle étudiant en supervisant ses prédictions sur des préfixes générés par sa propre politique, mais cette supervision se limite à l'espace des sorties. Elle ne transmet pas les mécanismes internes du professeur, ce qui empêche l'étudiant d'apprendre les processus computationnels intermédiaires menant aux prédictions, limitant ainsi son efficacité et sa généralisation.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs proposent l'On-Policy Mechanism Distillation (OPMD), une méthode qui va au-delà de la simple supervision des sorties en transférant les calculs intermédiaires du professeur tout en garantissant leur compatibilité avec l'étudiant. OPMD construit d'abord un *professeur compatible avec l'étudiant* en transformant les représentations intermédiaires du professeur pour qu'elles soient exploitables par les couches suivantes de l'étudiant. Ensuite, ces états intermédiaires sont internalisés via des trajectoires générées par la politique de l'étudiant (*on-policy*). Contrairement aux méthodes classiques de *representation matching*, OPMD évite les problèmes d'alignement géométrique entre les représentations du professeur et de l'étudiant, et s'assure que les états intermédiaires sont utilisables par la suite du pipeline computationnel de l'étudiant.
deep_analysis.resultats: OPMD obtient les meilleures performances moyennes parmi les méthodes de distillation évaluées, dans trois configurations différentes de paires professeur-étudiant. La méthode se généralise également à la distillation multi-professeurs et au *fine-tuning* supervisé entre familles de modèles différentes. Les analyses montrent que la supervision des mécanismes améliore le raisonnement de l'étudiant et modifie significativement ses calculs intermédiaires et ses stratégies de résolution, confirmant qu'elle transmet des informations au-delà de la simple supervision des sorties.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les détails techniques des transformations appliquées pour rendre le professeur compatible avec l'étudiant, ni les métriques exactes utilisées pour évaluer l'alignement des représentations. De plus, l'impact de la complexité computationnelle supplémentaire introduite par OPMD n'est pas discuté, ce qui pourrait limiter son applicabilité à grande échelle.
deep_analysis.verdict: Cette publication mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante visant à transférer les mécanismes internes des modèles, mais son adoption dépendra de la transparence des détails techniques et de son efficacité en pratique face aux coûts computationnels.

items.title: Belief-Trajectory Energy: Measuring the Path to a Prediction
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) progressively revise their predictions across Transformer layers, yet we typically observe only the final output, discarding the trajectory through which it is formed. We introduce Belief-Trajectory Energy(BTE), a model-grounded measure that characterizes an input through the layerwise predictive revisions it induces in a model. By mapping intermediate states into a shared predictive space, BTE provides a principled measure of belief change that can be summarized as either a scalar or a structured depth profile. Theoretically, we show that local BTE corresponds to predictive revision under the Fisher-Rao geometry, while the sequence of revisions captures information beyond the initial-to-final belief change. Empirically, scalar BTE provides a model-relative signal of difficulty across diverse reasoning tasks, while richer BTE representations support human-LLM review detection and fine-grained generator attribution, reaching up to 0.998 macro-AUROC and 95.6% eight-way attribution accuracy. Further analysis shows that BTE develops throughout pretraining and is selectively reshaped by targeted training, demonstrating that the resulting measurement reflects what the scoring model has learned. Together, our results establish belief trajectories as a principled model-grounded signal and suggest a broader perspective in which learned models can themselves serve as instruments for characterizing the data they process. More demonstrations can be found at https://yingjiahao14.github.io/BTE-web/.
items.tldr: Belief-Trajectory Energy (BTE) mesure les révisions prédictives couche par couche dans les LLMs, offrant un outil d'interprétabilité pour évaluer la difficulté des tâches, détecter les revues automatisées ou attribuer des générateurs. La méthode est validée théoriquement et empiriquement.

items.title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
items.summary: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.
items.tldr: Présentation d'Intact, un framework pour sécuriser les interactions des agents IA avec le web en préservant la sémantique des éléments (provenance, capacités) et en limitant les risques de manipulation via des attaques par injection de contenu tiers. L'approche repose sur une représentation structurée (GenTree) et une exécution contrôlée par l'utilisateur.

items.title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
items.summary: Decision models answer typed questions about an input with one probability per option, computed in a single forward pass without generating text. Like the fast System 1 of dual-process theory, they answer at once, but their depth is fixed at training time, so they spend the same computation on easy and hard questions. Models that reason in generated text can think longer, but they pay for every extra step in decoded tokens. We present LEV, a decision model that thinks deeper by rerunning its layers in a loop instead of generating tokens. LEV builds on a language model pretrained as a loop, reads the options after every loop step and trains all steps jointly, so one checkpoint can answer at any depth. On three looped backbones, accuracy rises with depth on the same weights, mostly on hard questions, and a 2.6B LEV goes from 63.2% at depth one to 76.2% at depth four on JevBench. On-demand depth, set per question by a small stopper with a threshold fitted on unlabelled requests, saves 15% to 24% of the computation at a cost of under one accuracy point, level with or slightly above a fixed mix of depths. On a locked test set, the 1.4B and 3B models are 5.4 to 8.8 points more accurate than dense (non-looped) models and cascades of the same latency below 50 ms.
items.tldr: LEV propose un modèle de décision en boucle (looped) qui améliore la précision avec la profondeur sans générer de tokens, économisant jusqu'à 24% de calcul pour une perte négligeable. Les gains sont maximaux sur les questions difficiles, avec une gestion dynamique de la profondeur.

items.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design
items.summary: Looped language models reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, but established architectures entangle recurrence placement, input injection, and recurrent state organization. We isolate these axes in models trained from scratch at matched parameter scale, logical depth, and token budgets, and then test whether the resulting design principles transfer to resident- and active-parameter-matched Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. The prelude-recurrent block-coda sandwich architecture consistently improves performance on context extraction and reasoning-intensive tasks. Input injection primarily enhances knowledge retrieval and context utilization, whereas random initialization and separate H/L recurrent states provide mixed or negative returns. Taken together, these results favor the Huginn-style design: at the 730M-parameter and 336B-token scale, the complete Huginn architecture outperforms Ouro across all ten benchmarks. The advantages of Huginn over Ouro transfer to MoE models. At the 8BA0.8B (32BA3B when unrolled) scale trained on 500B tokens, Huginn outperforms Ouro on nearly all benchmarks spanning knowledge, reasoning, and coding, while also exhibiting more balanced expert routing. Under matched training and inference FLOPs, the Huginn-style model uses 75% fewer resident parameters than a 112-layer feedforward MoE baseline. Despite its smaller physical parameters, it outperforms the feedforward baseline on DROP and GSM8K, matches it on MATH500, and remains competitive on the other benchmarks.
items.tldr: L'étude analyse l'impact de l'architecture des modèles en boucle (looped) sur les performances, isolant les axes clés (topologie, injection d'entrée, état récurrent). La conception Huginn surpasse Ouro sur 10 benchmarks, avec des gains transférables aux modèles MoE.

items.title: Selection Is Not Learning: Choosing Model Futures
items.summary: Self-evolving language models train on tasks they generate, so every round must decide which updated model the next round inherits. Current loops such as R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill Self-Play make this decision through the task, admitting tasks that look learnable and inheriting every resulting update. We identify a selection-to-update gap in these loops, where a task that looks learnable need not produce a useful update. Most updates on verified tasks fail to make correct answers more likely, yet these loops inherit them all. HeirCommit freezes the updated model and uses fresh evaluation questions to decide whether to inherit it or retain the current model. EvoHeir separates parameter inheritance from experience inheritance, using current and archived experience to repair failures and preserve successes before final confirmation. Our analysis characterizes selection-induced optimism and decomposes regret into selection, absorption, and confirmation errors. HeirCommit cuts the harmful share of accepted updates by 68-83% relative to random inheritance at the same acceptance rate. Across four backbones, EvoHeir achieves the best mathematics and general-reasoning averages, raising the math average by 5.3% relative to the strongest baseline, Agent0. The framework lets useful experience persist even when the model that produced it is not inherited.
items.tldr: Analyse critique des boucles d'auto-évolution des LLM (R-Zero, Agent0) qui révèlent un biais de sélection : les tâches perçues comme apprenables ne garantissent pas des mises à jour utiles. Présentation de HeirCommit et EvoHeir pour filtrer les mises à jour inefficaces, réduisant les mises à jour nuisibles de 68-83% et améliorant les performances en raisonnement mathématique et général.

items.title: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
items.summary: We introduce OpenMobile-2, a near-frontier mobile agent with fully open training environments and recipes. We make three key advances: (1) Diverse environments with simulated commercial apps: We build MobileGym++, featuring 35 realistic, functionally rich commercial-style apps with cross-app workflows, while preserving full controllability for reset and verification. Together with newly configured apps in Android emulators, this yields a diverse playground spanning over 110 apps. (2) Open training data at scale: Building on this foundation, we curate nearly 12K mobile interaction trajectories for supervised fine-tuning and the largest open collection of verifiable RL training data for mobile agents, comprising over 2K executable tasks with automatic rewards. (3) Hybrid GUI and app-native tool use: We explore an experimental mobile-use setting where apps expose selected functionalities as app-native tools alongside their GUIs, allowing agents to interleave GUI actions and tool calls within a task. We implement this setting in MobileGym++ with over 300 carefully scoped tools across 50+ apps. Additionally, we introduce MobileGym++ Bench for complex, long-horizon commercial mobile scenarios, supporting both GUI-only and hybrid GUI-tool evaluation on a shared task suite. OpenMobile-2 performs competitively across established benchmarks, including AndroidWorld (79.9) and MobileWorld (50.4), while showing promising transfer to real-device mobile use, nearly doubling SPA-Bench performance from 31.9 to 59.6. All resources are available at https://os-copilot.github.io/OpenMobile2-Home/.
items.tldr: OpenMobile-2, un agent mobile open-source avec 110+ apps simulées, 12K trajectoires d'interaction et 300+ outils natifs. Introduit MobileGym++ Bench pour évaluer les agents sur des scénarios commerciaux complexes et long-horizon avec des récompenses automatiques.

items.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
items.summary: The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does. We argue that every hidden state has a native reference frame, induced by the layers that read it next and adaptive to the context. Lexical reference frames approximate it by reading a state through the model's own remaining layers with a stated number of rounds of attention between positions and a typical attention output for the rest, without fitting to the model's output. No lens, with fixed directions per layer, can exceed the square root of the native frame's coherence, 0.30 and 0.35 at mid-depth of SmolLM3-3B and OLMo3-7B, whereas the first-order frame, LexFrame[1], reaches 0.97 and 0.97 and reads a state within 0.16 nats of the model's output. Its coefficients attribute predictions more faithfully than attribution patching, its lexical basis steers a prediction while sparing other tokens, and its confident readings would let an early exit skip 0.45 and 0.42 of the layers, where lenses skip almost none. In this way, lexical reference frames make every hidden state of the model readable, attributable and steerable.
items.tldr: Lexical Reference Frames propose une méthode pour interpréter les états cachés des LLM via des cadres de référence lexicaux, atteignant une cohérence de 0,97 avec les prédictions du modèle. Permet une attribution plus fidèle et un early exit efficace (jusqu'à 45% de couches sautées).

items.title: Stuck on Shuffle: On Attribute-Object Binding in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Retrieval is a fundamental task in multimodal systems: given an image or text query, the goal is to find the most relevant images or texts in a collection, often using a shared embedding space. Reliable retrieval requires these embeddings to capture not only which concepts are present, but also how they are composed. One key compositional challenge is attribute--object binding: encoding which attributes belong to which objects. Existing benchmarks provide a limited view of this capability, typically covering a subset of modality pairings, simple two-object swaps, or small attribute sets. Consequently, it remains unclear how robustly current models preserve attribute--object bindings across different modality pairings and more complex settings. We therefore introduce SABER, a controlled benchmark for evaluating attribute--object binding across all four image and text modality pairings, spanning diverse attribute types and scenes with up to ten objects. Evaluating models on SABER reveals substantial binding failures in both CLIP-style dual encoders and recent MLLM-based embedders. These findings motivate us to ask how binding can be improved efficiently. While multimodal supervision may be effective, collecting suitable images is difficult and costly. Text, on the other hand, is well suited to binding supervision: it is cheap to generate, supports a broader range of attributes and enables precisely controlled hard negatives. We thus finetune an MLLM-based embedder exclusively on synthetic attribute-binding text. Despite the absence of image supervision, the gains transfer to cross-modal and image--image retrieval while preserving general multimodal embedding performance. Our model achieves SOTA results on SABER while also improving on negation and instance-retrieval benchmarks, demonstrating broader benefits of our binding-focused supervision.
items.tldr: Le papier introduit SABER, un benchmark contrôlé pour évaluer la robustesse des modèles vision-langage (MLLM et encodeurs duals) dans la conservation des liens attribut-objet, révélant des faiblesses majeures en compositionnalité multimodale. Une analyse méthodique des échecs motive des pistes d'amélioration efficaces pour la supervision multimodale.

items.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
items.summary: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind. The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control. This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change. The same gap appears in general memory evaluations. On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction. Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score. On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%. The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.
items.tldr: Benchmark MIST pour évaluer la mémoire des modèles de monde vidéo, séparant la mémorisation de l'exécution des changements. M3-Agent, une méthode récursive, triple le score de révélation MIST et améliore les benchmarks WRBench (+26.1%) et MBench-T (+52.7%) en forçant l'exécution des instructions.

items.title: Consistent Distribution Matching for Data-Free Diffusion Distillation
items.summary: Flow and diffusion models suffer from slow inference due to computationally expensive numerical integration. Distillation provides a promising way for a student model to learn from a teacher's dynamics, enabling one-step or few-step generation. However, existing methods often depend on curated distillation datasets, costly teacher rollouts, or auxiliary proxy networks, which complicate model training and scaling. In this work, we propose Consistent Distribution Matching, a simulation-free and data-free distillation method for accelerating diffusion and flow models while preserving strong generative capacity. Our key insight is to unify sample generation and score estimation with one student network. Thus, our framework uses only two models, a frozen teacher and a trainable student, and optimizes one objective. We prove that minimizing our objective indicates Wasserstein convergence of the student flow-map pushforwards to the teacher marginals. On ImageNet 256times256, our method attains an FID of 2.04 with a single function evaluation (1-NFE) and a 4-NFE FID of 1.37 within 40 epochs of training, surpassing the state-of-the-art distillation baselines without data. Our code code and model are available at https://consistentdmd.github.io/.
items.tldr: Consistent Distribution Matching propose une méthode de distillation sans données pour accélérer les modèles de diffusion/flux (1-NFE à FID 2.04 sur ImageNet 256x256) en unifiant échantillonnage et estimation de score dans un seul réseau étudiant, avec preuve théorique de convergence de Wasserstein.

items.title: Dream2Discern: Learning from Hard Latent Variants for Runtime Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Reliable deployment of LLM-based multi-agent systems calls for runtime auditors that predict terminal outcomes from observed execution prefixes. These auditors typically learn from a limited corpus of trajectories with verified outcomes. Expanding this corpus requires costly execution and verification, yet broader failure coverage alone provides no explicit criterion for identifying prefixes that the current auditor finds difficult to classify. To this end, we propose Dream2Discern, a runtime auditor trained through implicit augmentation guided by its own prediction loss. During Dream, we select perturbations of the auditor's representation operators to increase prediction loss on recorded prefixes, yielding hard latent variants. During Discern, the auditor learns to predict execution outcomes from these variants using the original labels. The variants are regenerated as the auditor learns, turning a limited corpus into a renewable source of hard examples and requiring no additional trajectory collection or outcome verification. Extensive evaluations on AFTraj-2K and StepShield show that Dream2Discern outperforms competitive failure auditors and achieves over 90% trajectory-level weighted accuracy on both benchmarks while balancing prediction accuracy and timeliness. Project page: https://zbox1005.github.io/dream2discern-project/
items.tldr: Dream2Discern améliore les auditeurs de runtime pour systèmes multi-agents en générant dynamiquement des exemples difficiles via perturbations des opérateurs de représentation. Atteint >90% de précision sur des benchmarks comme AFTraj-2K et StepShield.

items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
items.summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.
items.tldr: OfficeTown simule des organisations professionnelles génératives où des agents coordonnent des tâches complexes avec persistance des artefacts et feedbacks. Benchmark de 406 tâches avec 4 836 critères, révélant des marges de progression significatives pour les modèles frontaliers.

items.title: FC-SWE: Failure-Conditioned RL for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents
items.summary: Repository-level software engineering (SWE) is a challenging long-horizon setting: agents must reason over extended interactions, use tools, and adapt to stateful environments. Recent work trains SWE agents with reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which independently sample multiple trajectories per issue, test the resulting patches, and compare terminal rewards within a fixed group. However, this training setup does not reuse verifier feedback from failed patches as context for subsequent attempts, even though this feedback contains valuable diagnostic information about what went wrong. Training on recovery trajectories is challenging because the preceding outcome determines whether the next trajectory is generated, while the failed execution determines its conditioning context. We introduce FC-SWE, a failure-conditioned RL framework that incorporates recovery attempts into policy training. After a patch fails verification, FC-SWE restores the repository to its original task state and uses the failed patch and verifier feedback as context for a recovery trajectory. FC-SWE adapts GRPO to these chains of complete, multi-turn tool-use trajectories through two mechanisms. Trajectory-local rewards preserve each attempt's verifier outcome, preventing recovery success from rewarding an earlier failed patch. Active-set advantage estimation forms a comparison group from all initial and recovery trajectories actually executed for the same issue, so failed attempts remain in the group while unexecuted attempts are excluded. On all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks under a verifier-assisted protocol, FC-SWE with Qwen3.5-4B and SWE-agent achieves 41.7% Resolved@1 and 52.8% Resolved@2, compared with 38.9% and 48.5% for GRPO. Although trained with at most two attempts per chain, FC-SWE reaches 70.7% Resolved@11 under an eleven-attempt test-time budget.
items.tldr: FC-SWE intègre les retours des échecs (feedback des vérificateurs) dans l'entraînement RL pour agents SWE long-horizon. Améliore l'efficacité des tentatives de récupération en réutilisant les diagnostics des patches échoués.

items.title: Skip the Compressor: Coding Agents Fix More Issues When They Pick Whole Files
items.summary: A coding agent works on repositories that can be far larger than its context window can hold. Prompt compressors and retrievers offer solutions to this problem, but patching an issue needs two things at once: the files that must change, and their code exactly as written, since the model must reproduce the lines it edits. Retrievers rank code by its similarity to the issue rather than by whether it must change, and compressors delete text to fit the budget. We show that at an equal token budget, an agent resolves more issues when the budget goes to choosing which files to show verbatim, as our simple selector CQ2-CARE does, than when it goes to pruning tokens or retrieving chunks. We fit every context to the same per-issue budget on 300 recent SWE-rebench issues and grade each patch with the benchmark's tests. With GPT-5.6 and Claude Opus 5, CQ2-CARE resolves 43.7% and 46.7% of the issues, 6.3 points more than the best of three compressors with either model, and 9.3 and 12.7 points more than the best of three retrievers. CQ2-CARE even resolves more issues than two methods trained for issue resolution, SweRank (by 0.7 and 1.7 points) and SWE-Pruner (by 2.0 and 7.3). Our analysis shows the defects of the baseline methods: retrievers often miss the files to edit, and compressors keep them but alter their text, so fewer patches apply. Exact-file selection needs no compression model and shows every line as the repository has it, so the model can quote the code it edits.
items.tldr: CQ2-CARE démontre qu'un agent de codage résout plus de problèmes (SWE-bench) en sélectionnant des fichiers entiers à afficher plutôt qu'en compressant ou récupérant des chunks, avec des gains significatifs vs. méthodes existantes (compresseurs, récupérateurs, modèles spécialisés).

items.title: DAGFormer: Global Topology Prediction for Transformer Cross-Layer Connections
items.summary: We propose DAGFormer, a Transformer language model whose cross-layer connections are planned by a jointly trained topology predictor. Beyond the residual connections in a standard Transformer, DAGFormer adds direct connections from earlier layers to later ones, and the predictor controls the strength of every connection based on input tokens. Unlike existing cross-layer routing architectures, which set each layer's connections separately, DAGFormer plans the routing of the whole model at once. On matched OLMo-2 pairs from 75M to 1B parameters, DAGFormer lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by 17% to 25% over the vanilla Transformer, and a 1B DAGFormer trained on 5B tokens outperforms the vanilla model trained on 10B. Against four routing baselines with the same data and budget, it reaches the lowest perplexity at 75M, 300M and 1B. The gain carries over to 13 commonsense, science, reading and math evaluation tasks (2.0 to 2.5 points higher mean accuracy at 300M and 1B) and to instruction finetuning (63% to 70% AlpacaEval win rate against the vanilla Transformer, leading every routing baseline), and under structured pruning DAGFormer degrades the least in five of six settings.
items.tldr: DAGFormer introduit un prédicteur de topologie pour optimiser les connexions inter-couches dans les Transformers, réduisant la perplexité de 17-25% vs. un Transformer vanilla et améliorant les performances sur 13 tâches de raisonnement. Les gains persistent sous pruning structuré.

items.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average 3.16times decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.
items.tldr: ReaDy, une méthode de *speculative decoding* exploitant les états récurrents des modèles HLA pour un contexte position-spécifique, accélérant la génération avec un overhead minimal. Améliore les performances sur 7 benchmarks avec une accélération jusqu'à 2.5x.

items.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer. To close this gap, we present Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4B MLLM built on Qwen3.5 that predicts masks from its own visual representations. Specifically, a lightweight decoder combines vision-encoder patch features with visual latents, the language model's mask-token states, so mask supervision reaches the shared backbone without an additional segmentation encoder. Because each latent decodes to a mask, the model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents and thus think with visual latents, while grounded reasoning traces supervise the regions it visits during chain-of-thought. As a result, across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits, Xiaomi-Lens-0 gains 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 in referring comprehension and achieves the highest segmentation cIoU among compared models. Moreover, it surpasses Qwen3.5 across all perception benchmarks. Homepage: https://seerray-lab.github.io/Xiaomi-Lens-0{this https URL}
items.tldr: Xiaomi-Lens-0, un MLLM de 4B (Qwen3.5) intégrant une supervision par masques pour améliorer la compréhension fine des régions d'images, avec gains significatifs en compréhension référentielle (RefCOCO) et en segmentation. Approche innovante pour l'interprétation visuelle guidée par le texte.

items.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
items.summary: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only as an environment with which the model can interact through actions (e.g., move left) and observations (rendered images). Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question. The model can then iteratively reason, navigate, and reorient its viewpoint before committing to a final answer. Following an initial trajectory-supervised finetuning, we apply reinforcement learning (RL) with rewards driven primarily by final-answer correctness. Crucially, RL provides no direct supervision over which viewpoints the model should visit or which exploration actions it should take. Instead, the model must learn an effective exploration policy solely from the extent to which its interactions improve performance. Across six 3D benchmarks, our model ACT3D achieves an average accuracy of 53.2% that improves its base Qwen model by 22.0% and surpasses proprietary Gemini 3.6 Flash. ACT3D also outperforms existing open-source 3D methods while using 50-70% fewer input frames, and generalizes to unseen domains with an average improvement of 5.9% over its supervised initialization. Further analysis reveals adaptive, question-conditioned exploration. Performance gains over the base model increase from 0.6% on questions answerable from the initial view to 16.3% on those requiring extensive exploration. ACT3D searches for occluded targets, avoids unnecessary exploration, and acquires complementary viewpoints for spatial comparisons. These findings demonstrate that outcome-based RL enables VLMs not only to reason over visual evidence, but also to learn when and how to acquire it.
items.tldr: ACT3D apprend à des VLMs à explorer activement des environnements 3D via raisonnement itératif et navigation, avec un gain de 22% en précision par rapport au modèle de base. Démontre une capacité d'exploration autonome sans supervision directe des actions.

items.title: SciΠvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can keep scientific experiments running for months with little human supervision, but reliable autonomous research also requires scientific judgment. Evaluating scientific judgment is difficult because research decisions are open-ended and depend on project context. We construct SciΠvot, a 248-case benchmark of scientific judgment based on human corrections. The benchmark draws on records from six months of research in which senior researchers ran LLM agents on 26 projects across six scientific fields and repeatedly intervened to correct the agents' research judgments. In each case, an agent chooses between the original LLM plan and the human-corrected alternative, using only the project record available before the correction as context. We compare LLM and human performance and examine the effects of reasoning effort, access to the project record, and reconsideration. At medium reasoning effort with the project record, models systematically prefer the original LLM plan over the human-corrected alternative. Four of five frontier models perform below chance on the selected cases. The highest accuracy in the project condition across the tested models and reasoning effort settings is 63.5%, compared with 73.4% for fresh researchers. At medium effort, every model achieves lower accuracy with the project record than without it, and reconsideration does not consistently improve overall accuracy. Even with a human-corrected alternative available, frontier models struggle with the selected research decisions, while SciΠvot supports systematic evaluation of scientific judgment for LLM agents.
items.tldr: SciΠvot évalue le jugement scientifique des agents de recherche autonome via 248 cas basés sur des corrections humaines. Montre que les modèles frontaliers performent systématiquement en dessous du hasard dans des conditions contrôlées.

items.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
items.summary: Can AI agents organize scientific investigations that lead to well-supported conclusions? To evaluate this capability, we introduce PhysClosureBench, a benchmark of 50 expert-verified, goal-specified research tasks spanning strong-field, attosecond, and neighboring physics areas. Each task specifies the research objective and essential scientific constraints, while leaving the agent to organize the investigation and determine how to generate and validate the evidence needed to answer the question. A 20-criterion Atomic Score measures local scientific accomplishment, while Research Closure (RC0--RC4) assesses how fully the investigation resolves the specified research question based on whether its indispensable evidence requirements and applicable scope conditions are satisfied. We evaluate seven frontier LLMs, where Claude-Opus-5 achieves the highest mean Atomic Score (6.29/10) but reaches RC4 in only 32.7% of attempts. Across the benchmark, 36.2% of attempts scoring at least 8/10 still fall short of RC4, while all seven models reach RC4 on substantially fewer tasks in all three runs than in at least one. Case-level analysis further illustrates how misinterpretation of generated results and unresolved physical applicability limits can lead to incomplete closure. Together, these results reveal a persistent gap between AI agents' local scientific accomplishments and their ability to achieve complete research closure.
items.tldr: PhysClosureBench évalue la capacité des agents à mener des recherches scientifiques autonomes avec des critères de clôture (RC0-RC4). Claude-Opus-5 atteint le score le plus élevé (6.29/10) mais seulement 32.7% de clôture complète (RC4), révélant des limites dans la validation des preuves.

items.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
items.summary: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) receive image-generation supervision that exposes them to visual information not fully documented in text. Can learning to generate images expand what pretrained models know? We introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), a controlled protocol that supplies new knowledge through image-generation training and tests its accessibility through text-only question answering. Across seven knowledge categories and three UMMs, we observe direct but uneven transfer from visual supervision to language. Motivated by these observations, we successively introduce Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image--Text Alignment, which connect generation and answering through shared knowledge and interleaved responses, respectively. Guidance on selected entities can improve knowledge access on other entities without QA supervision, with additional gains from interleaved alignment. Further analysis shows that knowledge correctly reproduced in images is often more accessible through text, although substantial gaps remain between the two forms of access. These findings support visual generation as a source of knowledge beyond textual supervision, and motivate joint investigation of training data design and model architecture to make this knowledge more broadly accessible.
items.tldr: L'étude montre que l'entraînement à la génération d'images dans des modèles multimodaux unifiés (UMM) transfère des connaissances non documentées en texte, améliorant l'accès à l'information via QA textuel. Des techniques d'alignement (textuel et interlacé) optimisent ce transfert.

items.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
items.summary: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks. They typically evaluate an audio-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes. We propose an event-centric evaluation framework that disentangles audio and visual events at the event level, analyzes each event independently, cross-validates relations across modalities, and aggregates the judgments into a coarse-to-fine, three-level consistency metric. The metric assesses global narrative harmony, event-level temporal synchronization, and fine-grained attribute alignment, providing a general formulation for audio-video consistency evaluation across diverse generation settings and cross-modal relations. We instantiate the metric as AVC-Reward, a trainable audio-video reward model. To evaluate the agreement between automatic judgments and human perception across generation paradigms and relation complexities, we construct AVC-Benchmark, which is primarily built from diverse positive and negative samples generated by various types of audio-video generation models. AVC-Reward achieves state-of-the-art alignment with human judgment among automatic methods, provides interpretable rationales that localize failures, and improves the audio-video consistency of a joint generation model when used as an online reinforcement-learning signal. Project page: https://tsuki0512.github.io/AVC-Reward.github.io/
items.tldr: AVC-Reward introduit un cadre d'évaluation centré sur les événements pour mesurer la cohérence audio-vidéo dans les modèles de génération multimodale, couvrant la narration globale, la synchronisation temporelle et l'alignement fin des attributs. Le modèle de récompense associé corrèle fortement avec les jugements humains.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) hold broad knowledge in one set of weights, but lack interpretability and trustworthy reasoning, especially in high-stakes use cases. A neuro-symbolic model, with its interpretable architecture and System 2 reasoning capacity, is a promising alternative if built at the scale of LLMs; however, its symbolic backbone is usually constructed with human effort, so existing neuro-symbolic models are bottlenecked by the scope of the symbol component and usually domain-specific. A data-driven method could instead build a larger symbolic system by aligning and merging existing ones. We target its first, foundational step: matching units across these heterogeneous systems. Our method, SAE-IDF, encodes a symbol in its native context into a sparse code with a sparse autoencoder (SAE), re-weights each dimension by its rarity and matches across systems. On 12 tasks across 6 kinds of symbolic system, SAE-IDF outperforms the same LLM's dense baseline on all tasks with Gemma-2-9B and all but one with Llama-3.1-8B, by up to 45 points, consistently across SAE layers and configurations. SAE-IDF is also interpretable: every dimension of the sparse code has a human-readable meaning, so each match decomposes into named concepts (features). Our work paves the way to a universal symbolic backbone.
items.tldr: SAE-IDF utilise des autoencodeurs clairsemés (SAE) pour aligner des systèmes symboliques hétérogènes en pondérant les dimensions par leur rareté. Améliore les performances de 45 points sur 12 tâches avec Gemma-2-9B et Llama-3.1-8B, tout en offrant une interprétation des dimensions.

items.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
items.summary: Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. First, each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discovers an optimization target and a fast, tailored proxy evaluator, which we call a yardstick. The agent then hill-climbs the yardstick rather than the true evaluation. Second, since search can exploit gaps between a yardstick and the true objective, fidelity tests continually recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift. Third, the fleet is bottom-up, with no central decomposition of the problem. A lightweight orchestrator spawns and terminates agents, briefs running ones, and seeds new agents with others' confirmed work. DuoDiscover enables autonomous optimization from software to chip architecture. We demonstrate DuoDiscover on two repository-level benchmarks and four GPU and TPU kernel suites covering hundreds of kernels. On SWE-fficiency, it doubles the average speedup of human experts. On SOL-Exec, it ranks first on 121 of 235 kernels and in the top three on 212. On the heavily optimized vLLM and SQLite engines, DuoDiscover achieves 1.92times and 1.38times gains over the base code. On a CPU microarchitecture optimization task with evaluations of up to 28 hours, DuoDiscover surpasses both AlphaEvolve-based ArchAgent v2 and the best human design, with 1.65times ArchAgent v2's gain in 16.7 days versus more than 40 days, advancing the frontier of autonomous chip design.
items.tldr: DuoDiscover, un système d'optimisation autonome où des agents co-découvrent des cibles et des évaluateurs proxy (*yardsticks*) pour accélérer la recherche. Utilise des tests de fidélité pour éviter les écarts entre proxy et objectif réel, permettant une optimisation logicielle autonome.

items.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
items.summary: Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality. However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes. In this work, we introduce Scene-Designer, an agentic framework that learns design intelligence through complementary design and critique experiences. We construct two datasets: Scene-OTA-35K, which provides Observation--Thought--Action supervision for learning scene design and efficient error correction, and Scene-OTC-15K, which provides Observation--Thought--Critic supervision for learning scene quality critique across physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence. Based on these experiences, we propose Scene-GRPO, a Critic-guided GRPO framework that improves design decisions and reduces unnecessary trial-and-error corrections. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Scene-Designer achieves superior performance in physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence, while the learned Scene-Critic significantly outperforms general-purpose models in scene critique. Moreover, test-time Critic guidance further improves scene generation, showing that the Critic can provide useful guidance beyond training. Additional analysis suggests a trend of mutual enhancement between scene design and critique abilities.
items.tldr: Scene-Designer introduit un framework agentique pour la génération 3D de scènes intérieures, combinant apprentissage par design (Scene-OTA-35K) et critique (Scene-OTC-15K) pour améliorer la validité physique, la fonctionnalité et la cohérence des layouts. Utilisation de GRPO guidé par un critique dédié.

items.title: MorphAct: Robot Policies Morphing with the Worlds They Act In
items.summary: Progress toward general intelligence in the physical world requires scaling robot learning across diverse environments and interactions. However, existing robot policies use shared parameters that remain fixed across interaction contexts. When different operations favor competing parameter adjustments, fitting their mixture can leave individual operations insufficiently adapted. Our atomic-task diagnostics reveal competing update directions in both vision-language and action parameters, with source-improving updates increasing loss on other tasks. This motivates MorphAct, a contextual parameterization framework that dynamically adjusts robot policy parameters as interaction contexts change. Two coupled generators produce context-dependent low-rank updates for the vision-language and action modules. Their coupling follows the policy's computational dependency: vision-language updates shape the representations that condition action-side parameter generation. Both generators are trained jointly through the native action objective, without operation labels or expert-adapter targets. MorphAct improves performance across three VLA backbones on LIBERO and Meta-World, with gains of up to 16.30%. In real-world evaluation, it achieves gains of up to 14% over π_{0.5}. Ablations support the benefits of contextual parameter generation and representation coupling.
items.tldr: MorphAct introduit une paramétrisation contextuelle dynamique pour politiques robotiques, adaptant les paramètres en fonction des environnements via générateurs couplés (vision-langage et action). Améliore les performances jusqu'à 15% sur LIBERO et Meta-World.
